context: These conclusions rest on treating the round keys as independent, so the classes we compute are classes of the pair (k, k 0 ) ranging over independent round keys rather than over master keys. For PRESENT this costs nothing: every class is realised by key-scheduleconsistent keys, each by exactly 250 master keys, so the classes, the weights ωi and the survivor counts are the same whether the round keys are treated as independent or derived from a master key. The mask space and its dimension d are unaffected in either case, being properties of the round function and the linear layer rather than of the key values. We have not checked the other ciphers, and the independent-round-key model remains an assumption for them. For those, the key schedule is better imposed natively—as a constraint inside the trail enumeration—than as a filter on the classes afterwards: a filter can only discard classes already computed, whereas a constraint keeps the enumeration from producing them at all. Several directions remain open. The SMT-based basis search is the runtime bottle- Tim Beyne, Gregor Leander, Mariia Mutkovina, Ricardo Rodriguez Reveco 31 neck; specialised solvers exploiting the vector-space structure of V0 (a) could push the method to ciphers with larger mask dimensions, such as Rectangle. Extending beyond bit-permutations to MDS linear layers requires only new SMT constraint encoding, though the growth of d under stronger diffusion is an empirical question. The method applies to any keyed permutation—not only the key-recovery map—and applying it to the forward cipher Ek would provide per-key distinguisher probabilities, the natural companion to the present work. Our tool is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22129299.
